proposed_from.topic: Primitive Shared-Center Rowwise-TV PSACE Frontier and Sign Radius across ACCT trials. For m≥4 randomized trials and q=4 states x,z=(S,Y), observe arm marginals μ_g^0 and ν_g and maintain the observable first-stage floor Δ_g^S≥κ>0. Define primitive stochastic center rows k_x and primitive trial rows k_gx for every state, interpreting k_gx as a conditional transition law only when μ_g^0(x)>0. Impose TV(k_gx,k_x)≤d for d∈[0,1] and exact marginal reproduction, with no latent entry floor. Prove compatibility iff Σ_g⟨h_g,ν_g⟩≤H_d^*(h) for every h, where H_d^* is the direct finite rowwise LP support; prove finite normalized facet sufficiency, polynomial-size LP separation, and rational feasible or Farkas certificates. Derive attained sharp PSACE intervals, the compatibility radius ρ*, and trialwise/all-trial sign-reversal radii with an attaining adversarial kernel, finite dual cut or rational infeasibility ray, including +∞. On the explicit nondegenerate m=4 observable neighborhood W_{ε_w}, prove {θ_1^WM}=Θ_1^pr(0)⊊Θ_1^pr(d)⊊Θ_1^ST for every 0<d≤10^-2, with Wu–Mao as the d=0 comparator. Prove simultaneous multinomial-region coverage by set inclusion, including ties, incompatibility, d∈{0,1}, and +∞. For rational numerical inputs, give finite exact CAD profiling of the bilinear projections; practical complexity, implementation, coverage-preserving rational outer approximation for generally irrational concentration radii, and the numerical ACCT reanalysis are not claimed.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: The theorem-level kernel is not abstract convex separation. It is the exact elimination of one shared strictly interior four-state stochastic center under trialwise TV perturbations: the feasible treatment-marginal set is a Minkowski sum whose support evaluates to the stated \(\eta\)-weighted sum--maximum term plus \(\delta\) times trialwise oscillation, and whose reverse direction is realized by broadcasting each zero-sum residual to every center row. This produces a finite normalized determining fan, polynomial separation with rational certificates, and constructive latent rows. On the same coupled polytope, attained PSACE ratios and single- and all-trial sign radii are new deterministic robustness objects. The closest 2025--2026 sensitivity papers vary regression transport or principal ignorability, not a shared multi-trial latent transition kernel. Simultaneous confidence-region inversion is valid by construction; globally certified bilinear profiling at ties and the extended-real branch is deliberately exposed as the open question rather than claimed solved.

seed_details.anchor: JiangDingGeng2016, Introduction, Theorem 1 and its mixture-equation proof, Sections 7--8; BeresteanuMolchanovMolinari2011, Theorem 2.1 and proof, Section 5
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace exact common stratum risks by one common interior transition center, then eliminate every trial-specific row through its zero-sum marginal residual before applying separation.
seed_details.destination_search: Targeted searches for principal stratification, multiple trials, shared stochastic kernels, total variation, support functions, and exact compatibility found Jiang--Ding--Geng and generic convex-capacity results but no shared-center TV theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Beresteanu--Molchanov--Molinari because every compact convex feasible set equals the intersection of its support halfspaces.
seed_details.rebuttal: Abstract separation is inherited, but the closed support formula and reverse direction require the new interior residual-broadcast lemma; without \(\eta>\delta\), adding a residual to every center row can leave the simplex.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The focal object is the closed-form support \(H_{\eta,\delta}\), not an unspecified LP image, and the theorem gives both necessity and constructive sufficiency.
seed_details.burned_reason: Angle 0 exhausted seven versions and the one authorized root-changing retry; the final cold review remained below field with non-PASS defects.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace point identification or simulated conditional-mean drift by joint linear-fractional optimization over the shared-center feasible polytope, then minimize the radius under numerator sign constraints.

proposed_from.literature_map: The selected kernel joins three adjacent threads. First, Jiang, Ding, and Geng (2016, Theorem 1, Proposition 2, Sections 7--8, and the proof of Theorem 1) use heterogeneous trial mixtures to identify PSACEs under exact conditional homogeneity, then replace violations by a hierarchical logistic-normal model. Beresteanu, Molchanov, and Molinari (2011, Theorem 2.1 and proof) show that sharp convex moment regions are characterized by support domination, while Galichon and Henry (2011, core theorem, matching theorem, submodular computation theorem, and core-determining theorem) show how finite capacity inequalities and constructive matchings can replace latent selection mechanisms. Neither paper evaluates the support of the present shared interior kernel plus trialwise TV residuals. Second, Charnes and Cooper (1962, Theorems 1--3) supply the ratio-to-LP move; Hsiao, Tian, and Parast (2025, Sections 2--3) supply the nearest resilience construction under regression drift; and Chen, Harhay, and Li (2026, Theorems 1--2) supply the newest sharp principal-effect sensitivity bounds and a falsification threshold under principal-ignorability violations. Their deviation classes do not couple multiple trials through one latent kernel. Third, Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019) give calibrated projection, Cho and Russell (2024, Theorem 2) give uniform perturbed-LP inference, and Fang and Santos (2019) diagnose ordinary-bootstrap failure for nondifferentiable maps. The exact destination remains open because jointly profiling multinomial control margins with transition rows produces bilinear products and the all-trial crossing functional can equal \(+\infty\). Weissman and coauthors (2003) make conservative simultaneous region inversion available without active-face smoothness, and McCormick (1976) gives the first global-optimization handle rather than a solution to that profiling problem.
